rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 2 (score 600.6, best so far) finishes the oval 20/20 (mean finish 1.94 s), finishes the s-bend 13/20, and never finishes the slalom (0/20). Slalom runs end off track at progress 0.28 with max_error 0.0638, just above the fixed 0.06 m limit, and about 1 line-loss event per run. Iteration 2 added the forward sensor shift (y 0.06), mass 0.6 kg, kp 3.0, kd 0.7 and base_speed 1.4. The Evaluator's note on the 1.4 speed is stale: the oval finished at 1.94 s, so the speed margin is large. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at 0.06 for any allowed body width, so the robot must keep max_error under 0.06 by control alone.

Changes. (1) base_speed 1.4 to 1.3. Slalom and s-bend losses look like speed-dependent drift through sharp direction changes, and the oval has time margin to absorb a lower speed (the 3 s limit is about 1.94 s at 1.4). (2) kd 0.7 to 0.8. Slalom alternates left and right, so extra derivative damping should cut overshoot between bends; oval oscillation (0.25) is well below the 0.3 concern. Geometry, kp 3.0, ki 0.05, sensor_weights and line_loss ('last_direction') are unchanged, so the race isolates speed plus damping against iteration 2.

Expected result. Slalom progress rises and some slalom runs finish; s-bend finish rate stays at or above 0.65; slalom line_loss_events fall toward 0.7 or below; oval still finishes in under 3 s (about 2.1 to 2.3 s expected). Hypotheses: (a) lower speed reduces bend drift enough to keep max_error below 0.06 on the slalom; (b) kd 0.8 reduces overshoot without raising oval oscillation above about 0.3. If the oval finish fails, return base_speed to 1.4. If the slalom still ends off track with max_error above 0.06, next try kp 2.6 at base_speed 1.2, or kd 0.9.
